transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad to meet you today. What brings you in to see me?
I've been making a lot of careless mistakes lately because I find it really hard to pay attention to details. I also feel this constant sense of restlessness, like I just can't sit still.
Have you experienced these difficulties with attention and restlessness since you were a child, or is this something that started more recently in your life?

These issues aren't new at all; I've actually struggled with this since I was a kid, definitely before I turned 12. More recently, this constant struggle has been going on for about two years and four months now.
Along with the restlessness, do you experience constant, excessive worry about everyday things that you find difficult to control?
No, I don't really experience constant or excessive worry about everyday things. While I definitely feel restless a lot of the time, I don't have trouble with uncontrollable worrying.
Aside from feeling restless, do you often find yourself acting impulsively, such as interrupting others, blurting out answers, or having trouble waiting your turn?
No, I don't really experience those kinds of behaviors. I haven't noticed myself interrupting people or blurting out answers, and waiting my turn isn't usually an issue for me.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting with your hands or feet, squirming in your seat, talking excessively, or feeling like you are constantly "on the go"?

I don't really fidget with my hands or talk excessively, but I have a really hard time actually staying in my seat when I'm expected to. I just get this intense feeling of restlessness inside that makes me feel like I need to get up and move around.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates included both Combined Presentation and Predominantly Inattentive Presentation of ADHD. However, the patient has now explicitly denied most hyperactive and impulsive symptoms (denying fidgeting, excessive talking, interrupting, blurting out answers, and difficulty waiting turns), endorsing only restlessness and difficulty staying seated. Since they do not meet the full criteria for the hyperactive/impulsive component (which requires at least 5 symptoms for adults), the Combined Presentation is ruled out, leaving Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation) as the sole candidate.
